required_outcomes: Identifies that the receipt (bought 9 March 2023 with a 2-year manufacturer guarantee) puts the oven inside the manufacturer's warranty until March 2025, which contradicts Harbour's 'no longer under warranty' (most likely their own 12-month fitting warranty).

Tells Harbour Services the guarantee details and asks them to treat tomorrow's visit as diagnosis only and to route the repair through a Calder warranty claim (or confirm whether Calder must attend), with no chargeable work without approval.
Replies to the landlord confirming that the manufacturer's guarantee is being pursued and that no chargeable repair will be authorised without him.
Updates the tenant on tomorrow's visit (Wednesday 22 May, 2:30pm) and that the repair may be done by the manufacturer under warranty, which can take longer.
acceptable_alternatives: Contacting Calder directly, or asking the landlord to register the claim, instead of going through Harbour, provided Harbour is told not to carry out chargeable work.
Cancelling Harbour's visit in favour of a manufacturer engineer, provided the tenant and Harbour are told and the manufacturer booking is under way.
positive_behaviours: Asks the landlord for a copy of the receipt so it can go to the manufacturer.
Records the purchase date and the guarantee term on the case.
red_flags: Escalating to a human when the landlord's receipt settles the question.
Repeating Harbour's out-of-warranty view to the tenant or landlord as fact.
prohibited_actions: Authorising a chargeable repair or replacement.
Assigning a second provider or creating a duplicate request.
critical_failures: Approving spend or instructing a chargeable repair when the landlord's receipt shows the oven is inside a 2-year manufacturer guarantee.
